speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry has conducted any studies on the effect stacked ranking has on teachers collaborating with each other; (b) if so, what do the results of these studies show; and (c) whether the Ministry will conduct such studies if it has not done so.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The system allows us to consistently identify and recognise stronger performing officers, while at the same time provide development opportunities to those who need more support to help them improve their performance.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In addition, the system also helps to moderate differences in supervisors’ assessments and establish common standards of performance assessment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We adopt a holistic approach in assessing our teachers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They are expected to be able to deliver effective teaching and pastoral care, support students in their character development, interact well with students and contribute to the learning of fellow teachers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our teachers are also assessed on their ability to work and collaborate with others.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Apart from feedback from our School Leaders, MOE monitors key staff-related indicators like staff collaboration through our internal staff engagement surveys, and we do not find any particular concerns raised about our teachers not being able to collaborate with one another.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singapore Secondary school teachers who participated in OECD’s Teaching and Learning International Survey 2018 said that beyond performance ratings, they receive feedback that has a positive impact on their teaching practices.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, they reported that the teaching fraternity here has a strong collaborative and collegial culture, driven by a shared belief in collective improvement of practice.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: While there are ranking guidelines to adhere to, there is also flexibility for deviations, taking into consideration the performance of individual officers and specific circumstances.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Beyond the ranking guidelines or even the system of performance management that is in place, what is important is for our school leaders to continue motivating and inspiring our teachers to stay true to their calling as educators and help our students reach their full potential.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One is that we actually have done away with class ranking because we said that learning is not a competition.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why then do we make teaching a competition?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Does the Minister agree with me that by ranking teachers against each other, it might make them compete against each other and collaborate less as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know there are some survey results that show that a percentage feels that they can collaborate but I am just wondering whether ranking does help to move the needle towards making them compete against each other.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Two, can I ask whether MOE has studied this issue in terms of whether it benefits the students?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, does ranking the teachers actually benefit the students?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Teaching is a very demanding job; it is a special calling.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I know this from first-hand experience because my mother was a teacher for more than 40 years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, let us make no pretence of it.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is demanding, and I would say it is probably more demanding now than it used to be.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But it is also vitally important in bringing out the best in every child and nurturing the next generation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we spare no effort in building a first-rate teaching force, high quality and dedicated.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We also do our very best to support them in their work.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I say this because we have to look at appraisal systems in this context.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: An appraisal system is meant to enhance teaching quality.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Evidence around the world shows that having a good appraisal system can help in enhancing teaching quality.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: An OECD study said, for example, that "teacher appraisal can be a key lever for increasing the focus on teaching quality".

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, that is what we have been trying to do.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not about competition amongst the teachers, but it is putting in place an appraisal system where there is focus on quality and where the school leadership teams can continually assess their teachers, and identify the excellent teachers amongst them who can be the next generation of school leaders and master teachers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think that is important for maintaining that quality of our teaching force and also important in being able to nurture our next generation well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have been doing this for many years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have an appraisal system that works reasonably well and we have, as a result of it, a strong high-quality teaching force.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to review and improve the system, as I have said, based on feedback from all stakeholders and looking at experiences in other countries as well as best practices in other jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our fundamental objective is really to ensure a high quality teaching force and do the best for every child in our schools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Perhaps, the way to square this circle is to understand that maybe the concern is about ranking which potentially by its nature pits one teacher versus another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I wonder if there could be a move toward more of a measurement system that does not rely on ranking per se but focuses more on teachers actually just having reached absolute standards.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This does not penalise those who are very good teachers but may end up being ranked lower just by virtue of their peers being even better teachers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: How to go about designing this appraisal system?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think we have a system that works reasonably well, but I would be the first to acknowledge that it is not perfect.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I do not think there are perfect solutions anywhere in the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, there is, in that selection, some form of ranking inevitably but the purpose is to be able to identify the high performing ones so that you can nurture them and put them up for advancement, and then they can in turn be the next generation of school leaders and master teachers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We remain open with regard to new ideas and inputs on how this appraisal system can continue to be enhanced.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But our objective, I think all of us here in this House share that same objective, is to have an appraisal system that is fair, enhances teaching quality and helps us to advance the next generation of school leadership so that we can continue to do the best for our students.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I just want to reaffirm that I do agree that we should have an appraisal system as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But could I ask the Minister, he mentioned earlier that MOE is studying alternative appraisal models.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, could the Minister share what some of these models are that MOE is currently studying?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is an on-going process, Mr Speaker, because we continue to review this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And then we also see some of the negative experiences in other jurisdictions where sometimes if you put too much weight on one indicator, then the teachers teach to that or perform to that indicator only, and then you end up with inadvertent consequences.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Like I said, there is no perfect appraisal system anywhere in the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the end, you have to keep on improving, reviewing, updating and being mindful of the potential downsides.
